events_chronological: On the hottest morning of the year a disc jockey opens his broadcast from a storefront window on the block.
A young man gets out of bed at his sister's flat and goes off to deliver pizzas.
The pizzeria owner opens up with his two sons, the elder saying he hates the neighbourhood and everybody in it.
The block's old drunk buys his first beer of the day and is scolded for it by a woman watching from her window.
A regular objects that the photographs on the pizzeria wall are all of the owner's own countrymen and asks where the black faces are.
The owner throws him into the street, and he starts calling for a boycott that nobody joins.
A big quiet man walks the block all day with a boombox playing one song at full volume.
Three older men sit under an umbrella opposite a Korean grocery and talk about the block from morning until night.
A stammering man works the corner selling hand-coloured photographs of two murdered leaders.
The delivery man tells the owner's elder son to his face that every one of his heroes is black.
The old drunk pulls a child out of the path of a car, and the woman at the window softens towards him.
The hydrant is opened and the whole block plays in the water until a police car pulls up.
The big man and the boycotter come into the pizzeria at closing with the radio at full volume, demanding the wall be changed.
The owner smashes the boombox with a baseball bat and the fight spills into the street.
Police arrive and kill the big man with a chokehold in front of the entire block.
The delivery man throws a rubbish bin through the pizzeria window and the crowd burns the place down.
In the morning he comes back for his week's wages, and the two of them argue over the money among the ashes.
nonlinear_category_reason: Every strand keeps its own forward order and nothing is ever shown out of turn in time; the inversions are only between strands running at the same moment, which the telling cuts between sideways. One block, one hot day, a dozen strands, and no scene anywhere out of its hour.
syuzhet_notes: The telling covers one day on one block, cutting between a dozen people who are all out in the same heat. The order is simply the order of the hours.
fabula_notes: Everything falls between one morning and the next. Where two strands share an hour, either ranking would serve.

events.content: From a storefront booth, the broadcaster names the heat and supplies a public voice that will accompany the block until night.

reader: the story is confined to one exceptionally hot day on one block
